clue.text: 50% of Middle Easterners least affected by sun?

indicators.note: fifty per cent means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: Palestinians are people of the Middle East

explanation.surface: A survey asks which Middle Eastern people tan least.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone least affected by sun stays the most pallid, the least tanned of all.

clue.text: Don't buy off the peg, to get 'suited'

definitions.meaning: to have clothes tailored is to be measured, read as a two-word phrase
suited means appropriate, as in a gesture well matched to the occasion

explanation.surface: Advice to have a suit tailored rather than bought ready-made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suited to an occasion was appropriate to it, the same sense as fitting.

clue.text: Check behind nest — no way — animal's grabbed that bird

indicators.note: the animal holds the other letters in its grip, a container signal

parts.note: a stoat is a small animal of the weasel family

indicators.note: behind places the check abbreviation after the trimmed nest
no means the way abbreviation is taken out of nest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A bird's nest is raided by a predator that seizes the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as a verb about inspecting the nest, but it is the chess abbreviation; 'no way' trims the nest to NE before the animal grabs it.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European songbird of the chat family.

clue.text: Academic introduces, after vacation, notable writer

indicators.note: the academic comes first, introducing what follows

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: vacated means emptied of its inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A university teacher back from holiday introduces a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notable writer' looks like the definition, but 'notable' loses its middle to give NE.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet, a writer of verse and sermons.

clue.text: Indian official rejected limitless trade with S American capital

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the combined letters read in reverse
without limits, the word trade loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Lima is the capital city of Peru

explanation.surface: An Indian bureaucrat turns down unrestricted commerce with Peru's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: RAD from 'trade' plus LIMA makes RADLIMA, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An amildar was a revenue collector or local administrator in British-era India.

clue.text: One saves on exotic cruise — first person goes free

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so the letters are rearranged
the first person is released from the word, leaving it out

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone saves money on a foreign cruise and a passenger travels free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' looks like it describes the cruise, but it is the anagram signal, working on CRUSE once the first person is freed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer is one who saves people from danger.

clue.text: Old actor Flynn perhaps recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Errol Flynn was a Hollywood actor, so Errol is an example of a Flynn

explanation.surface: Errol Flynn, the old film star, is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flynn perhaps' hints at a surname, but it is the first name Errol that gets turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Lorre was a Hungarian-born film actor of the 1930s and 1940s, famous for menacing roles.

clue.text: Outsize women go over garments daughter rejected

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the little word is read backwards
the daughter is rejected, taken out of the garments

parts.note: dresses are garments

explanation.surface: Large women look at frocks that a daughter turns down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogresses are female giants of folklore, monstrous women of huge size.

clue.text: Inspiration among the Great Plains?

parts.note: in means among, as in one in a crowd
the Great Plains are the flat interior of the United States, read as flat US

explanation.surface: A question about where a person finds creative inspiration out on the prairies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Plains of North America are the flat region of the US, so they read as FLAT US.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflatus is a rare word for a breathing in or a divine afflatus, an inspiring breath.

clue.text: Endless fortune attracting an ancient poet

indicators.note: attracting means drawing the next word on to it, joining it at the end
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: luck is good fortune

explanation.surface: A fortune without limit draws in an old poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucan was a Roman poet of the first century, author of the Pharsalia.

clue.text: Party organiser, say, to turn up shortly carrying wine

indicators.note: carrying means holding the wine inside
shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: to invert something is to turn it upside down
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A party host arrives briefly with a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wine' here is Italian vermouth, the IT of a gin and it; 'shortly' leaves INVER to carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who invites guests is a host, so a party organiser is an example.

clue.text: Deny going round women's prison

indicators.note: going round means surrounding the letter for women

parts.note: to negate is to deny
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Someone denies anything happens around a women's jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'women's prison' looks like one phrase, but 'women's' supplies W and 'prison' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904.

clue.text: Do you like alternative names? Primarily a Welsh one?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A question about whether you enjoy unusual names, perhaps a Welsh one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan is a traditional Welsh boy's name, borne by the poet Dylan Thomas.

clue.text: Don't stop magazine senior keeps taking regularly

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the magazine sits within the senior abbreviation

parts.note: The Oldie is a British monthly magazine
to be on a medicine is to take it regularly

explanation.surface: A magazine for older readers stays in a pensioner's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oldie is a British humorous magazine for older readers.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to keep going despite difficulty, an idiom for not stopping.

clue.text: List includes bill for car

indicators.note: includes means the list contains the bill within it

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty
an ad is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A list of expenses includes a bill for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadster is an open two-seater car.

clue.text: Do get stuffed after starchy starter … of this?

definitions.text: Do get stuffed after starchy starter … of this?

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the first letter
the starter of a word is its first letter
stuffed suggests something crammed and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner is told to fill up on heavy food after a starchy first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' rearranges DO GET into TODGE, after the S of starchy; the whole clue also describes heavy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling starchy food, the kind that leaves one stuffed.

clue.text: Secretary's fur wrap likely to win approval

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary, with the possessive s
a sable is a fur, worn as a wrap

explanation.surface: A secretary's fur stole is sure to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passable is acceptable, good enough to win approval.

clue.text: Not so stable toilet needs supporting structure

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A rickety lavatory needs propping up.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy means crazy, so loopier is less mentally stable, a comparative of the slang sense.

clue.text: Plant, drug source

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A plant that is the origin of a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small plant with blue flowers, genus Veronica.

clue.text: Go into work, quashing rebellion with show of resourcefulness

parts.note: to enter is to go into

indicators.note: quashing means pressing down on, the work surrounding the rebellion

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
a rising is a rebellion

explanation.surface: Workers go in and put down an uprising with great initiative.
explanation.definitionFit: To act enterprisingly is to act with initiative and resourcefulness.

clue.text: Wind usually crushes flower

indicators.note: the two words crush the answer between them, holding it within

explanation.surface: A gale normally flattens blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword slang for a river, something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is something that flows, here the Indus, a great river of Pakistan.

clue.text: Hair not sticking up of course

indicators.note: in a down clue sticking up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: sure means of course, certainly

explanation.surface: Of course the hair isn't standing on end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's head with its ring of hair.

clue.text: Flat ready for refurbishment? Builder finally moves in

indicators.note: moves in means the letter enters the rearranged word
refurbishment means rearranging, so the letters of ready are reworked
finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An apartment needs doing up before a builder can move in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, but it means dull; R from 'Builder' joins the rearranged READY.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lifeless is a synonym of dreary.

clue.text: Dessert is tart encased in flaky crust, see

indicators.note: encased in means the tart is held inside the other letters
flaky means crumbly, so the letters break up and rearrange

parts.note: tart is slang for a harlot

explanation.surface: A dessert of tart wrapped in pastry is being offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like the pastry dessert itself, but it is slang for a prostitute; 'flaky' makes CTERUSSE to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte russe is a cold dessert of custard or cream set in sponge fingers.

clue.text: Very depressed fellow's little time for card game

parts.note: so low means very depressed
his means belonging to a fellow
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gloomy man has little time for a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a card game for four players, a variant of whist.

clue.text: Person held in empty edifice receiving bird

indicators.note: receiving means taking the bird inside
empty means the middle is removed, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone is imprisoned in a deserted building where a bird has landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' looks like part of the definition, but 'in' gives letters; 'empty' leaves EE of edifice to join it.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is a person confined, held without trial, often in wartime.

clue.text: Little work and lack of holiday accommodation? Dire, ultimately, for one

indicators.note: for means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: no means a lack of, as in no money
a villa is a holiday home
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Finding no holiday villa is a dire result.
explanation.walkthrough: NO VILLA has its I replaced by E, the end of 'Dire'.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a small piece of literary work.

clue.text: Burnt vegetable picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A scorched vegetable is lifted off the grill.
explanation.definitionFit: Charred means scorched or burnt black.

clue.text: Embarrassed-looking writer held up folder

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: red is the colour of an embarrassed face
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A blushing author raises a folder.
explanation.definitionFit: A binder is a ring folder for holding papers.

clue.text: Tension as interpreted by students?

parts.note: to means in the opinion of, as in to me
the NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: A question about how students understand tension.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonus is the slight continuous tension of a resting muscle.
